title: Cooper Test Provides Better Half-Marathon Performance Prediction in Recreational Runners Than Laboratory Tests
claims: Twenty-three recreational male runners completed a laboratory incremental test, the Cooper field test and a half marathon at maximal effort.
Half-marathon time correlated with Cooper test distance (r = -0.93, p < 0.001) and with speed at maximal oxygen uptake in the laboratory (r = -0.84, p < 0.0001).
The Cooper test distance was the best single predictor of half-marathon time, with R-squared 0.873 and standard error of estimate 3.78 minutes.
The authors state that these data may only be extrapolated to recreational male runners.

verification.note: Frontiers 开放获取全文（CC BY），已读摘要、方法、结果与讨论，含 Participants/Cooper Test 细节与局限性句。

claimVerification.note: 原文：“Twenty-three participants ... underwent ... a maximum incremental graded exercise laboratory test”；“Cooper's original protocol was performed on an athletic track”；“all participants completed a half-marathon race at the maximum possible speed”；Participants 节：“23 amateur male athletes”。

原文：“Significant correlations were found between the time in the half marathon and the distance in the Cooper test (r = −0.93; p < 0.001) ... speed reached at maximum oxygen consumption (vVO2max), (r = −0.84; p < 0.0001)”。数值一致。
原文：“The distance covered in the Cooper test was the best predictor of time in the half-marathon ... (R2 = 0.873, SEE: 3.78 min)”；实验室模型 R2 = 0.77、SEE 5.28 min，故“best single predictor”成立。
原文：“it is important to note that these data may only be extrapolated to recreational male runners.” 与 claim 语气一致。
